title: Expression and purification of ATP13A4 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae
author: Sarah van Veen
materials: Break the yeast cells using a BeadBeater.

steps.title: Plate yeast stock
steps.instruction: Plate the glycerol‑stock of Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4743 on a YPD‑agar plate and incubate for 48 h at 30 °C.

steps.title: Inoculate overnight culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate 20 mL YPD medium from the fresh plate and incubate overnight at 30 °C with shaking at 230 rpm.

steps.title: Measure overnight OD
steps.instruction: Measure the optical density at 600 nm (OD₆₀₀); 1 OD₆₀₀ ≈ 1 × 10⁷ cells · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Dilute to mid‑log phase
steps.instruction: Dilute the overnight culture to 0.1 OD₆₀₀ in 10 mL YPD and incubate 4–6 h at 30 °C, 230 rpm until the OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.4–0.8.

steps.title: Harvest cells for transformation
steps.instruction: Spin down cells equivalent to 2 OD₆₀₀ (≈2 × 10⁷ cells) in swinging‑bucket rotors at 700 × g for 5 min (temperature not specified).

steps.title: Wash and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet with 1 mL sterile milliQ water, resuspend with a pipet tip, transfer to an Eppendorf tube, spin at 2 500 × g for 2 min, resuspend in 1 mL 1× TE/LiAc, spin again at 2 500 × g for 2 min, and finally resuspend in 100 µL 1× TE/LiAc.

steps.title: Add DNA and PEG
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL single‑stranded herring‑sperm DNA (prepared by boiling for 20 min and cooling on ice), add 1–5 µg plasmid DNA (pYSG‑IBA162‑FLAG‑hATP13A4‑TwinStrep), vortex, then add 600 µL PEG solution, vortex again.

steps.title: Incubate and add DMSO
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture for 45 min at 30 °C (total volume ≈ 730 µL), then add DMSO to a final concentration of 10 % (≈ 73 µL).

steps.title: Heat‑shock and recover
steps.instruction: Heat‑shock at 42 °C for 15 min, cool on ice for 1–2 min, spin at 2 500 × g for 2 min, resuspend the pellet in 200 µL YPD and incubate 2 h at 30 °C, spin again at 2 500 × g for 2 min, resuspend in sterile milliQ water and plate onto MM‑uracil agar.

steps.title: Select transformants
steps.instruction: Incubate the selection plates for 48 h at 30 °C, pick colonies and grow each in 20 mL MM‑Ura medium at 28 °C, 175 rpm for 24 h.

steps.title: Large‑scale expression induction
steps.instruction: Collect the 20 mL pre‑culture by centrifugation at 1 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, resuspend the pellet in 4 L MM‑Leu medium, add 1 mM CuSO₄ to induce ATP13A4, and grow 24 h at 28 °C, 175 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest expression cells
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of the pre‑culture, inoculate 4 L MM‑Ura to a final OD₆₀₀ of 0.05, grow overnight at 28 °C, 175 rpm, then centrifuge at 1 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, weigh the pellet, and either use immediately or store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Thaw frozen pellets (if needed)
steps.instruction: If the pellet was frozen, thaw it in a water bath at 37 °C.

steps.title: Prepare bead‑beating chamber
steps.instruction: Fill the chamber with 200 mL yeast suspension (add TES buffer if volume is insufficient) and add 200 mL cold glass beads; the chamber should be as full as possible.

steps.title: Resuspend in TES buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in TES‑in buffer; use a volume (mL) approximately equal to the weight of the pellet (g) as determined in the previous step.

steps.title: Spin and resuspend in TEKS
steps.instruction: Spin at 1 000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, then resuspend the pellet in TEKS buffer using a volume (mL) ≈ 2 × pellet weight (g) and incubate 15 min at 4 °C while mixing with a magnetic stirrer.

steps.title: Extract crude lysate and adjust pH
steps.instruction: Recover the crude extract with a Büchner funnel and vacuum pump, test the pH with pH paper, and if necessary adjust to pH 7.5 with saturated NaOH solution.

steps.title: Bead‑beat cell suspension
steps.instruction: Bead‑beat in a cold room for 5 min, pausing 3 min after each minute to avoid heating; keep the ice‑water jacket filled with crushed ice and water.

steps.title: High‑speed clarification
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the supernatant at 200 000 × g, 4 °C, 1 h; discard the pellet, then centrifuge the supernatant at 20 000 × g, 4 °C, 20 min; finally centrifuge the resulting crude extract at 2 000 × g, 4 °C, 20 min.

steps.title: Separate membrane fractions
steps.instruction: Resuspend the light‑membrane pellet (P3) in HS buffer using the minimal volume required for a homogeneous solution; separately resuspend the heavy‑membrane pellet (P2) in HS buffer, also using the minimal volume.

steps.title: Small‑scale expression culture
steps.instruction: Measure OD₆₀₀ of a pre‑culture, inoculate 200 mL MM‑Ura to a final OD₆₀₀ of 0.2, and grow 12 h at 28 °C, 175 rpm.

steps.title: Determine membrane protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of the membrane fractions by a Bradford assay using BSA standards; typical concentrations are 20–50 mg · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Store membrane fractions
steps.instruction: Aliquot the membrane fractions, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂, and store at –80 °C (maximum storage time 6 months).

steps.title: Solubilize membranes
steps.instruction: Stir the membranes with a magnetic stirrer for 1 h at 4 °C to solubilize.

steps.title: Clarify solubilized membranes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the solubilized sample at 200 000 × g, 4 °C, 1 h to remove insoluble material.

steps.title: Bind to Strep‑Tactin resin
steps.instruction: Incubate the clarified supernatant with Strep‑Tactin® XT resin for 3 h at 4 °C in 50 mL Falcon tubes using a head‑over‑head rotator.

steps.title: Wash resin
steps.instruction: Wash the resin 5 times with 20 column volumes of SSR buffer.

steps.title: Elute ATP13A4
steps.instruction: Elute the bound protein with SSR buffer supplemented with 50 mM biotin (fractions E1–E5).

steps.title: Analyze purification quality
steps.instruction: Run SDS‑PAGE of the elution fractions and visualise by Coomassie staining or immunoblotting.

steps.title: Estimate protein by gel
steps.instruction: Estimate protein concentration by running an SDS‑PAGE gel with BSA standards and staining with Coomassie dye (as performed by Sarah van Veen).

steps.title: Dilute membranes for downstream use
steps.instruction: Dilute membranes to 5 mg · mL⁻¹ in SSR buffer containing 5 mg · mL⁻¹ DDM.

steps.title: Equilibrate Strep‑Tactin resin
steps.instruction: Wash the Strep‑Tactin® XT resin with 10 column volumes of SSR buffer at 300 × g, 4 °C, 3 min; use 0.5 mL beads (1 mL slurry) per 400 mg total protein (total resin volume = 1 column volume).

steps.title: Perform sequential elutions
steps.instruction: Elution 1: add 600 µL elution buffer, collect eluate (E1) and pour the mixture into a large column for gravity flow. Elution 2: add 1 600 µL elution buffer, incubate 5 min at 4 °C with head‑over‑head rotation, collect eluate (E2). Elution 3: add 800 µL elution buffer, incubate 5 min at 4 °C, collect eluate (E3). Elution 4: add 800 µL elution buffer, incubate 5 min at 4 °C, collect eluate (E4). Elution 5: add 800 µL elution buffer, incubate 5 min at 4 °C, collect eluate (E5). Combine fractions E2–E5 in one tube (E1 usually contains no protein), aliquot all fractions, flash‑freeze, and store at –80 °C.
